DocMind — Public Demo Test Document
A self-contained document for demonstrating PDF question answering, retrieval, multi-hop reasoning, and
numerical extraction.
1. Project Overview
DocMind is a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) document assistant designed to answer questions
from uploaded documents. For the public demo, a pre-indexed demonstration document is used so visitors
can ask questions without uploading or processing a new PDF on the hosted backend.
2. Demonstration Project: Aurora Analytics
Aurora Analytics conducted a six-week evaluation of its internal document-search assistant. The evaluation
compared three retrieval configurations: Baseline Search, Hybrid Retrieval, and Hybrid Retrieval with
Reranking. The goal was to determine whether combining keyword and semantic retrieval could improve
answer quality while keeping response latency acceptable.

3. Evaluation Setup
The evaluation used 1,200 questions created from a collection of 300 internal documents. Each configuration
was tested against the same question set. The team measured retrieval recall, answer accuracy, and median
response latency. A successful answer was defined as one that contained the required information and did
not contradict the source document.

4. Key Findings
• Hybrid Retrieval improved retrieval recall from 71% to 84%, a gain of 13 percentage points over Baseline
Search.
• Hybrid Retrieval with Reranking achieved the highest retrieval recall at 91% and the highest answer
accuracy at 87%.
• The reranked configuration increased median latency to 2.3 seconds, which was 0.5 seconds slower than
Hybrid Retrieval without reranking.
• The team considered 2.5 seconds an acceptable media

• The team considered 2.5 seconds an acceptable median latency for the internal use case.
• The evaluation suggested that the additional latency from reranking was justified by the improvement in
answer quality.
5. Implementation Notes
The demonstration system stores pre-processed document chunks and their vector representations before
deployment. During a user query, the system retrieves the most relevant chunks and passes them to the
language model as context. This reduces server-side work during the public demo because PDF parsing,
chunking, and indexing do not happen for every visitor.
6. Conclusion

For the Aurora Analytics evaluation, Hybrid Retrieval with Reranking provided the strongest overall retrieval
and answer-quality results. Although it introduced additional latency, the 2.3-second median remained within
the team's 2.5-second target. The results support using reranking when answer quality is more important
than minimizing latency.
